sections.content: In natural conversation, short markers organise turns, check that the listener is following and show attitude. You know *o sea* for reformulation from B2 Unit 29. Across all varieties of Spanish, six core pan-Hispanic markers carry everyday talk: *pues* opens an answer or draws a consequence (*Pues, no estoy seguro*); *bueno* accepts a point or shifts topic (*Bueno, cambiemos de tema*); *mira / mire* and *oye / oiga* call attention (*tú* vs *usted*); *¿no?* and *¿verdad?* seek agreement at the end of a turn; and *vamos* sums up or clarifies a conclusion (*Vamos, que no viene hoy*). You will also hear regional markers — Spain *vale*, *venga*, *hombre*; Mexico *órale*, *¿mande?*; River Plate *che*, *dale* — which are useful to recognise, though pan-Hispanic markers work everywhere.

sections.title: Pan-Hispanic spoken markers by function
rows: Starts an answer or draws a consequence (*Pues, la charla empezó tarde.*).
Accepts a point, softens a pause or shifts topic (*Bueno, volvamos al trabajo.*).
Calls the listener's attention (*tú* vs *usted*: *Oiga, una pregunta.*).
Reformulates (*o sea*) or sums up (*Vamos, que no pudo venir.*).
Seeks agreement or confirmation at the end of a statement.

items.spanish: Pues, después de la pausa, el entrevistador cambió de tema.
items.english: Well, after the break, the interviewer changed the subject.

items.spanish: Bueno, si todos están de acuerdo, empezamos la charla ahora.
items.english: Well then, if everyone agrees, let's start the talk now.

items.spanish: Oiga, ¿me permite aclarar ese punto antes de pasar a otra pregunta?
items.english: Excuse me, may I clarify that point before moving to another question?

items.spanish: No contestó ningún mensaje en toda la semana; vamos, que no quiere participar, ¿verdad?
items.english: He didn't answer a single message all week; in short, he doesn't want to take part, right?

sections.content: Avoid overusing a single filler (*muletilla*) like *o sea* in every sentence, and match *mira / oye* (*tú*) versus *mire / oiga* (*usted*) to your register. Regional markers (*vale*, *órale*, *che*, *dale*) are great to recognise in listening, while *bueno*, *pues*, *o sea*, *vamos* and *¿verdad?* sound natural across the whole Spanish-speaking world.
